title: Eddie Flaisler — 'I don't think I ever needed a book as badly as I did this one'
summary: Eddie Flaisler — VP Engineering at Uber, Box, and Lob — releases a People Driven Development podcast episode translating Incorruptible's framework into an actionable model for engineering leaders navigating the AI era. 26 likes on LinkedIn.
blockquote:
Four weeks ago, in the midst of all this uncertainty, Eric Ries — the father of The Lean Startup — released Incorruptible, his latest book. I don't think I ever needed a book as badly as I did this one. Something to remind me that putting mission and people first as a leader isn't being "soft" or "detached from business reality". It's being an expert strategist.

In this episode, Morgan VanDerLeest and I take a few key principles from Eric's book and translate them into an actionable framework for engineering leaders navigating the AI era. We use concepts from managerial economics to understand how to measure (and not measure) AI effectiveness, how to think about the different aspects of structural integrity, and how to approach the present moment in a way conducive to what we're trying to achieve.
attribution_title: VP Engineering — Uber, Box, Lob; Creator of Mission Control (AI Intelligence for Engineering Leaders)
